note: Every word in the app that is not UI copy lives here. An occasion may carry a `yours` object, used when the day is the reader's own rather than their partner's; blank it back to TODO and the card falls back to the shared line above it rather than to nothing. These are drafts in the app's own voice, written to be replaced — rewrite any of them and nothing else has to change. Anything reading TODO is unwritten and will not ship: packages/core/src/dedication.test.ts fails on it, and occasionCopy() returns null rather than showing a placeholder on somebody's anniversary.

signature.line: Built for one person, then opened up.

colophon.title: What this is
colophon.opening: A small shared space for two people. Everything in it is free and always will be — there is no paid tier to find later, no advertising, and nothing here is counting you.

promises.title: It stays free
promises.body: Every question pack, every widget, every game. There is no tier above this one.

promises.title: Unpairing really deletes
promises.body: Both of you confirm, and then the photos, the drawings, the answers and the letters are gone from the server and from the phone. Afterwards the app asks what survived and tells you if anything did.

promises.title: Location is off until you turn it on
promises.body: Each of you decides separately and either can switch it off without telling the other first. It is read only while the app is open, rounded to roughly your city, and the most it ever shows is how far apart you are — never where either of you is.

promises.title: Your answer is yours until they answer too
promises.body: Neither of you can read the other's reply to the day's question, or their pick in a game, before writing your own. That is enforced by the database rather than by this app politely looking away.

promises.title: You can take all of it with you
promises.body: One tap in Us gives you a file with every row and every picture, at full size, that opens without this app existing.

promises.title: Nobody is watching
promises.body: No analytics, no tracking, no third parties. The fonts are served from here rather than borrowed from somewhere that would learn you had opened it.

birthday.eyebrow: day one, for one of them
birthday.line: They started today. Nothing else here would be here otherwise.

yours.line: Somebody has had today circled for weeks. It is not you.

milestone.line: You were not keeping score. It went up anyway.

monthly.line: It came round. It will keep coming round.

minute.line: The clock just said your date back to you.

counter.held: hours — the same thing said in a way that sounds like more
quotes: Every one of them had you in it.
Nobody counted at the time. It counted anyway.
The ordinary ones are the ones this is made of.
You have been somebody's favourite thing for all of them.
Long enough to have forgotten most of it, and kept the rest.
None of them were promised. All of them happened.
Somewhere in here is the day you stopped being nervous.
A number that only goes one way, which is the whole point.
Enough hours to have learned how they take their tea.
Most of them were nothing much. That is the good news.
You could have spent them anywhere. You spent them here.
Still adding up, quietly, while you are not looking.

hers.note: Only ever shown to one person, or to the couple she is half of. See packages/core/src/dedication.ts for how each is decided, and read the comment there before adding to this — it is obfuscated, not secret.
hers.line: The K is me and the S is you. There was never a version of this that was about anything else.
questions: What is the smallest thing the other one does that you would miss most?
When did you first think this might be serious? Be specific about the room.
What do you know about them that they have never said out loud to anyone?
